reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of spatial perception emerges from the inherent variability of sensory experience across body regions. Each sensation carries an intrinsic topographic signature—its 'feeling shade'—which is independent of conscious awareness. This suggests a latent kernel of spatial information encoded within the sensory modality itself. The susceptibility of sensations to localization implies a probabilistic framework where spatial attribution is not immediate but conditional upon further cognitive development. In GSI, this manifests as a prior over spatial coordinates derived from sensory input. In GSE, it enables dynamic state transitions from raw tactile data to structured spatial cognition. The failure mode occurs when this susceptibility collapses into uniformity, indicating loss of spatial resolution or perceptual degradation. The duality lies between the immediate sensory quality and its abstracted spatial representation, both necessary for full conscious understanding.
